title: Akashvani Bhawan | Kolkata Trips
description: Discover Akashvani Bhawan Kolkata, the headquarters of All India Radio in Eastern India. Learn its history, architecture, location, nearby attractions.
textContent: Akashvani Bhawan Akashvani Bhawan is one of Kolkata’s most recognizable government buildings and an important landmark in the city’s broadcasting history. Located in the heart of Central Kolkata near Eden Gardens and the Maidan, it serves as the regional headquarters of All India Radio (AIR) for Eastern India. Although not a conventional tourist attraction, the building holds immense historical and cultural significance, particularly for those interested in India’s evolution of radio broadcasting. Visitors passing through the heritage district of Kolkata often notice its imposing modernist architecture and strategic location amidst many iconic colonial-era landmarks. Quick Information Information Details Location Eden Gardens Area, Kolkata Established Mid-20th Century Managed By Prasar Bharati – All India Radio Famous For Radio broadcasting headquarters Entry Fee Not open for regular public visits Photography Exterior only Time Required 10–15 minutes (Exterior) Nearest Metro Esplanade / Maidan History of Akashvani Bhawan Kolkata The history of radio broadcasting in Kolkata dates back to the late 1920s. Kolkata became one of the earliest cities in India to embrace radio communication, playing a pioneering role in the country’s broadcasting network. Following India’s independence, radio became an essential medium for: National news Educational programming Classical music Folk traditions Drama Public awareness campaigns To accommodate expanding broadcasting operations, Akashvani Bhawan was established as the headquarters for All India Radio’s eastern services. Over the decades, the building has witnessed major national events, elections, cultural festivals, and countless historic broadcasts that reached millions of listeners across Eastern and North-Eastern India. Many renowned musicians, writers, poets, and public figures have visited its studios to record performances and interviews. Why is it Called “Akashvani”? The Sanskrit word “Akashvani” literally means “Voice from the Sky.” The name was adopted as the Indian identity for All India Radio and became synonymous with trustworthy public broadcasting across the country. For generations of Indians, hearing the words: “Yeh Akashvani Hai…” became an instantly recognizable introduction to radio news broadcasts. Architecture and Design Unlike many colonial buildings nearby, Akashvani Bhawan represents India’s post-independence government architecture. Its design emphasizes functionality rather than ornamentation. Key architectural features include: Clean modernist façade Large office spaces Soundproof broadcasting studios Administrative offices Recording rooms Transmission control facilities Multiple broadcasting wings Although the building appears relatively simple from the outside, it houses sophisticated radio production infrastructure that has evolved significantly over the decades. Importance of Akashvani Bhawan Akashvani Bhawan has played a crucial role in preserving India’s cultural heritage through radio. Some of its contributions include: Broadcasting Rabindra Sangeet Classical Hindustani music Bengali literature readings Educational programmes News bulletins Agricultural information Cultural discussions Emergency public announcements It has helped preserve countless recordings of legendary artists, scholars, and performers. Famous Personalities Associated with All India Radio Kolkata Over the decades, numerous distinguished personalities have been associated with Kolkata’s All India Radio studios, including: Rabindranath Tagore (special broadcasts) Satyajit Ray Hemanta Mukhopadhyay Manna Dey Suchitra Mitra Birendra Krishna Bhadra Debabrata Biswas One of the most cherished annual broadcasts remains Mahishasuramardini, narrated by Birendra Krishna Bhadra, which continues to be aired before Durga Puja and is deeply woven into Bengali cultural tradition. Can Visitors Enter Akashvani Bhawan? Generally, no. The building functions as an active government office and broadcasting center. Public entry is usually restricted except: Official appointments Government work Educational visits (with prior permission) Special broadcasting events Visitors can, however, admire the exterior while exploring nearby heritage attractions. Timings Since it is an operational government office: Office Hours: Monday to Friday (Government office timings) Public Entry: Restricted Exterior Viewing: Anytime from the surrounding roads Entry Fee Exterior viewing: Free Public access inside: Not generally permitted Best Time to Visit The best months are: October November December January February Pleasant weather makes it comfortable to explore the surrounding heritage district on foot. Morning and late afternoon also offer excellent lighting for photography. How to Reach Akashvani Bhawan By Metro Nearest stations include: Esplanade Maidan Both are within walking distance. By Bus Numerous city buses connect Esplanade, B.B.D. Bagh, Howrah, and Park Street. By Taxi Taxis and app-based cabs are readily available throughout Kolkata. By Train Nearest railway stations: Howrah Junction Sealdah Station Both are approximately 5–7 km away. Nearby Attractions Akashvani Bhawan is surrounded by several of Kolkata’s most iconic landmarks, making it an easy stop during a Full Day Kolkata City Tour. 1. Eden Gardens One of the world’s most famous cricket stadiums. 2. Maidan Kolkata’s vast green expanse known as the “Lungs of Kolkata.” 3. Fort William Historic British military fort (exterior viewing only). 4. Victoria Memorial The city’s most celebrated monument and museum. 5. St. Paul’s Cathedral A magnificent Gothic Revival cathedral. 6. Raj Bhavan Official residence of the Governor of West Bengal. 7. Town Hall A heritage building showcasing Kolkata’s colonial history. 8. Writers’ Building One of Kolkata’s most iconic administrative landmarks. 9. General Post Office (GPO) A grand colonial structure in B.B.D. Bagh. 10. Shaheed Minar Historic monument overlooking the Maidan. Visitor Tips The building is not a tourist monument. Photography is best done from public roads. Security personnel should not be disturbed. Combine your visit with nearby heritage attractions. Visit during daylight hours for better views. Public entry requires prior authorization. Comfortable walking shoes are recommended when exploring the surrounding heritage district. Interesting Facts Kolkata is one of India’s oldest radio broadcasting centers. Akashvani Bhawan serves as the eastern regional headquarters of All India Radio. The building continues to broadcast multiple regional language programmes. Countless legendary musicians have recorded here. The famous Mahishasuramardini programme has been associated with All India Radio Kolkata for decades. The building remains an active broadcasting center today. Why Include Akashvani Bhawan in Your Kolkata Tour? Although visitors cannot usually enter the building, Akashvani Bhawan is an important landmark in Kolkata’s cultural landscape. It represents India’s broadcasting heritage and stands amidst many of the city’s most significant colonial-era monuments. For history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, and those exploring the heritage precinct around the Maidan and B.B.D. Bagh, it adds historical context to a walking or driving tour of central Kolkata. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. What is Akashvani Bhawan Kolkata famous for? It is the regional headquarters of All India Radio in Eastern India and an important center for public broadcasting. 2. Can tourists enter Akashvani Bhawan? No. Public entry is generally restricted unless prior permission has been obtained. 3. Is there an entry fee? No. Viewing the exterior is free. 4. Where is Akashvani Bhawan located? It is located near Eden Gardens and the Maidan in central Kolkata. 5. Why is it called Akashvani? “Akashvani” means “Voice from the Sky” in Sanskrit and is the Indian name for All India Radio. 6. Which famous personalities recorded here? Many renowned personalities, including Hemanta Mukhopadhyay, Manna Dey, Suchitra Mitra, Satyajit Ray, and Birendra Krishna Bhadra, have been associated with All India Radio Kolkata. 7. What is the famous Mahishasuramardini broadcast? It is an iconic devotional radio programme narrated by Birendra Krishna Bhadra and broadcast every year before Durga Puja. 8. What is the nearest metro station? Esplanade and Maidan Metro Stations are the closest. 9. How much time should I spend here? Around 10–15 minutes is sufficient for viewing the exterior as part of a heritage drive or walking tour. 10. What attractions are nearby? Victoria Memorial, Eden Gardens, Maidan, Fort William, Raj Bhavan, Town Hall, Writers’ Building, General Post Office, Shaheed Minar, and St. Paul’s Cathedral are all nearby. 11. Is photography allowed? Photography of the building’s exterior from public areas is generally permitted, but avoid photographing security-sensitive areas or personnel. 12. Is Akashvani Bhawan included in Kolkata sightseeing tours? Yes. Many Full Day Kolkata City Tours pass by Akashvani Bhawan while covering the city’s historic administrative and colonial landmarks.
